column2: 劉兄、どうして擂台に上がってみないんだ？
column3: Brother Liu, why don't you get up there and give it a try?

column2: 李兄、からかわないでください…。私に少しでも武芸の心得があれば、とっくに従妹の月如に求婚していますよ。
column3: Brother Li, please don't tease me... If I had learned even a little martial arts, I'd have asked for my cousin Yueru's hand long ago.

column2: どういうことだ？劉兄は礼儀正しくて品があるし、見た目だって立派じゃないか。その月如とかいう従妹があんたを気に入らないなら、そりゃ見る目がないってもんだぜ。
column3: How so? You're courteous, refined, and a fine-looking man besides. If this cousin Yueru of yours doesn't fancy you, she's got no eye for men at all.

column2: しっ…擂台の上に聞こえてしまいますよ。
column3: Shh... don't let her hear you up there.

column2: へえ？もしかして擂台の上にいるのが、劉兄の従妹の月如なのか？
column3: Oh? Don't tell me the one up in the ring is your cousin Yueru?

column2: へへ…劉兄がそこまで気にかけるんだ、さぞかし美人なんだろ？
column3: Heh... if she's got you this smitten, she must be quite a beauty, eh?

column2: どれどれ…。おおっ、なかなかやるじゃないか！
column3: Let me see... Whoa, she fights pretty well!

column2: ふん！だらしないわね。
column3: Hmph! Useless.

column2: ちょっと！まだ殴られたい奴はいるの？上がってきなさいよ！
column3: Hey! Anyone else itching for a beating? Get up here!

column2: 父さん！こいつら、まともなのが一人もいないじゃない。ちっともおもしろくないわ、もう帰りましょうよ。
column3: Father! Not one of these fellows is any good. This is no fun at all. Let's just go home.

column2: 如児！お前はいくらなんでも手加減がなさすぎるぞ。挑戦者は腕を折られるか、目を潰されるかじゃ。これでは誰も上がってこんわい。
column3: Ru'er! You hit far too hard. Every challenger ends up with a broken arm or a blinded eye. Who would dare come up now?

column2: またあたしのせい？あたしは女の子なのよ。この男どもがだらしなさすぎるのよ！
column3: Blaming me again? I'm a girl, you know. It's these stinking boys who are useless!

column2: 父はお前が婿を選べるよう、再三機会を作ってやった。どれだけ心を砕いたと思っておる？それなのにお前は一度たりとも真剣になったことがない。
column3: Time and again I've arranged chances for you to choose a husband. Do you know how much trouble I've gone to? And not once have you taken it seriously.

column2: そんなことないわよ、自分で見てみなさいよ！下にいる男たちはみんなびくびくして縮こまってるじゃない。あんなのが林家の婿にふさわしいと思う？
column3: That's not true. See for yourself! Every man down there is cringing and cowering. How could any of them be fit to marry into the Lin family?

column2: お前！…あーっ、あの乱暴娘！！
column3: You! ...Ahh, the wild girl!!

column2: よく覚えててくれたわね、まぬけなコソ泥！どうしたの、今日もまたあたしを縛り上げて木に吊るすつもり？
column3: How good of you to remember me, you thieving blockhead! Well? Planning to tie me up and hang me from a tree again today?

column2: お二人は知り合いなのですか？
column3: You two know each other?

column2: いや！前にちょっとした誤解があっただけだ。
column3: No! We just had a little misunderstanding earlier.

column2: 父さん！こいつよ、昨日あたしをいじめたのはこいつなの！ここに上がらせてよ、ぶちのめしてやるんだから。
column3: Father! That's him. He's the one who bullied me yesterday! Make him come up here. I'm going to give him a thrashing.

column2: 如児、わがままを言うでない！
column3: Ru'er, stop being willful!

column2: 知らないわよ、とにかく上がらせて。絶対にこの鬱憤を晴らしてやるんだから！
column3: I don't care. Make him come up. I will get even with him!

column2: 確かに先に無礼を働いたのは私の方です。ですが、自分から進んであなたの剣を一太刀受けたのですから、もう貸し借りなしのはず。お嬢さん、そこまで人を追い詰めることはないでしょう？
column3: It's true I wronged you first, Miss, but I willingly took a stroke of your sword, so we're even. Why push a man so hard?

column2: 納得いかないわ！昨日はあんたたち二人がかりであたし一人を相手にしたじゃない。今日は度胸があるなら一対一で勝負しなさいよ。
column3: I won't accept that! Yesterday it was the two of you against me alone. If you've got the guts, fight me one on one today.

column2: はは！一度負けたくせに、まだ痛い目に遭いたいのか？
column3: Haha! I've beaten you once already. Are you asking for more?

column2: あんたが勝ったら、あたしたちの間のいざこざは帳消しにしてあげる。でも負けたら、うちで一年間下働きをしてもらうわ。あんたが逃がした銀花と長貴の分の埋め合わせよ！どう、怖じ気づいた？
column3: If you win, the score between us is wiped clean. If you lose, you work as a laborer in my house for a year, to make up for Yinhua and Changgui, whom you let get away! Well? Scared?

column2: 言ったのはそっちだからな！俺が勝ちさえすれば、昨日のことは帳消しなんだな？
column3: Those are your words, mind you! If I beat you, yesterday's business is wiped clean?

column2: そうよ！
column3: That's right!

column2: 如児！ふざけるでない！
column3: Ru'er! This is no game!

column2: 父さん、口を出さないでよ！今日みんなの前で面目を取り戻さなかったら、蘇州の林家堡が人に侮られちゃうじゃない。
column3: Father, stay out of it! If I don't win back my honor in front of everyone today, people will look down on the Lin Family Fort of Suzhou.

column2: よしよし…お前の好きにするがいい。ただし、寸止めまでじゃぞ、分かったな？
column3: All right, all right... have it your way. But stop short of doing real harm, understood?

column2: ふふ…構えなさい！
column3: Hee... show me your moves!

column2: 参ったわ…。
column3: I yield...

column2: 勝ちを譲ってもらって、どうも。
column3: Thanks for going easy on me.

column2: 擂台の下から拍手が沸き起こった。
column3: Applause breaks out below the ring.

column2: あ…ありがとう、皆さんありがとう。
column3: Ah... thank you, thank you, everyone.

column2: ほっほっほ…めでたい！実にめでたい！皆の衆、本日、娘の婿選びの試合にようやく決着がついた。皆の衆のご参集、まことにかたじけない。明日よりこの林、林家堡にて三日間の宴を開く。皆々様、ぜひともお越しくだされ！
column3: Ho ho ho... splendid! Splendid! Good people, today my daughter's tournament for her hand has at last produced a result. I thank you all for gracing the occasion. Starting tomorrow, I, Lin, will hold a three-day feast at the Lin Family Fort. Friends and elders, you must do me the honor of coming!

column2: 父さんったら！もう、知らないんだから…
column3: Father! Oh, I won't stand for this...

column2: はっはっは！珍しい、珍しい。如児が恥じらうこともあるとはのう。
column3: Hahaha! A rare sight, a rare sight. Who'd have thought Ru'er could blush?

column2: ど…どういうことだ？
column3: Wh... what's going on?

column2: ほっほっほ…若いの、何をそこでぼんやりしておる？如児の後を追わんか！
column3: Ho ho ho... young man, what are you standing there gaping for? Go after Ru'er!

column2: 俺が！？…なんで？
column3: Me!? ...Why?

column2: まだとぼけるか！？婿選びの擂台で如児に勝ったからには、お主は当然わが林家の婿じゃ。
column3: Still playing dumb!? You defeated Ru'er in the ring at a tournament for her hand, so naturally you are now the son-in-law of the Lin family.

column2: えええーっ！！！
column3: Whaaat!!!

column2: 李少侠はその若さでこれほどの腕前、剣術はまことに精妙、容姿もまた抜きん出ておる。少侠を婿に迎えられるとは、娘は果報者じゃ。ほっほっほ！
column3: So young, Young Hero Li, and yet so skilled. Your swordplay is exquisite, and your looks are outstanding too. To have you as a son-in-law is truly my daughter's good fortune. Ho ho ho!

column2: 私はただ運が良かっただけで…実は…
column3: I was only lucky... the truth is...

column2: そうじゃ、先ほどお主が使った剣法…あれは蜀山仙剣派の御剣術ではないか？
column3: By the way, that sword technique you used just now... was it the Sword Command of the Mount Shu Immortal Sword Sect?

column2: はい…。
column3: Yes...

column2: なんと、お主は独孤剣聖の弟子であったか。ほっほ、これはまた奇遇じゃ。わしとお主の師とは十数年来の義兄弟でな、言ってみればお主はわしの甥弟子にあたるのじゃよ。
column3: So you are a disciple of Sword Saint Dugu! Ho ho, what a coincidence. Your master and I have been sworn brothers for more than ten years. By that reckoning, you are my martial nephew.

column2: 独孤…剣聖…？い…いや、違います！
column3: Dugu... Sword Saint...? N-no, that's not right!

column2: ほう！違うのか？
column3: Oh! You're not?

column2: 正直に申しますと、私は縁あって、ある酔いどれ道士から剣法を一手授かっただけなのです。弟子入りしたかったのですが、叶いませんでした。
column3: To be honest, by a stroke of fate a drunken Taoist taught me a single sword technique. I wanted to become his disciple, but it wasn't to be.

column2: ほう…師匠はおらんのか？構わん、そんなことは大したことではない。わしが気にかけておるのは、お主と如児の婚儀じゃ！わが林家は三代続いて一人っ子、そしてわしには如児という娘が一人おるだけ。それゆえ、お主には林家に婿入りして、わが林家の家業を継いでもらいたいのじゃ。
column3: Oh... no master? No matter, that's of little importance. What concerns me is your marriage to Ru'er! For three generations the Lin family has had but a single heir, and Ru'er is my only daughter. So I wish you to marry into our family and inherit the Lin estate.

column2: 私にはとても務まりません！
column3: I couldn't possibly accept such an honor!

column2: おじ上、お待ちください！月如を彼に嫁がせるなんて！
column3: Uncle, wait! How can Yueru marry him?

column2: 何がいかんのじゃ？
column3: And why not?

column2: 私に武芸ができないとご存じのうえで、武芸の試合で月如の縁談をお決めになるなんて。
column3: You know full well that I have no martial arts, yet you decide Yueru's marriage by combat.

column2: 婿選びの試合である以上、擂台での勝負はすでについた…。
column3: It was a tournament for her hand, and the ring has decided the winner...

column2: いいえ！こんなものは無効です。月如の一生の大事を、こんなに軽々しく決めていいはずがありません！
column3: No! This cannot count. Yueru's whole future can't be settled so carelessly!

column2: そうだ！無効だ…
column3: Right! It doesn't count...

column2: 黙れ！月如はわしの娘じゃ。お前に何の資格があって口を挟む？
column3: Silence! Yueru is my daughter. What right have you to object?

column2: 私は…どうか月如を私にください！近いうちに父に頼んで、正式に縁談の使いを寄こします。
column3: I... please give Yueru to me! In a few days I'll have my father send someone to make a formal proposal.

column2: 月如はお前のことなどまるで好いておらん。ましてや一介の書生に、どうしてわしの南武林盟主の座が継げようか？
column3: Yueru doesn't care for you in the least. Besides, how could a mere scholar inherit my seat as leader of the Southern Martial World?

column2: 私は………
わ…分かりました…
column3: I... I understand...

column2: 李兄、あなたと月如の幸せを祈っています…
column3: Brother Li, I wish you and Yueru every happiness...

column2: おじ上、月如に私からの別れをお伝えください…私は都へ帰ることにします。
column3: Uncle, please say farewell to Yueru for me... I have decided to return to the Capital.

column2: 劉兄…！
column3: Brother Liu...!

column2: これで決まりじゃ！ほっほっほ…少侠を婿に迎えられるとは、まことに娘の果報じゃ。
column3: Then it's settled! Ho ho ho... to have you as a son-in-law is truly my daughter's good fortune.

column2: 私はお嬢様との間に少々誤解があったから、擂台に上がって手合わせしただけです。婿入りの…この件は、どうかご再考ください。
column3: I only stepped into the ring because of a small misunderstanding with your daughter. As for this marriage... I beg you to think it over, sir.

column2: もしや少侠は娘が気に入らぬと？
column3: Can it be that you find my daughter wanting?

column2: 申し訳ありません。私にはまだ大事な用があるのです。それに結婚は遊びではありません。軽々しくお約束して、お嬢様を裏切ることになってはと…。
column3: I'm truly sorry. I still have urgent business to attend to, and marriage is no trifling matter. I dare not make a rash promise, for fear of failing the young lady.

column2: 妻を娶るより大事な用などあるものか？
column3: What could be more important than taking a wife?

column2: 逍遥お兄ちゃん…もし、あなたが…わたし…一人で苗疆へ行けます。わたしのことは気にしないで…大丈夫ですから。
column3: Brother Xiaoyao... if you... I... I can go to the Miao lands by myself. You needn't worry about me... it's all right.

column2: そんなわけにいくか！お前を苗疆へ連れていって母さんを捜すって約束したんだ。簡単に約束を破れるかよ！
column3: Out of the question! I promised to take you to the Miao lands to find your mother. How could I go back on my word?

column2: わたし…お兄ちゃんの足手まといに…
column3: I... I've been a burden to you...

column2: 出ていくと申すか！まさか婚約を破るつもりか？わが林家に婿入りすることの、どこが不満じゃ？
column3: You mean to leave! Do you intend to break the engagement? What is so wrong with marrying into my family?

column2: 私は試合に勝って、約束どおり誤解を解きたかっただけで、結婚のことまでは考えてもいませんでした。
column3: I won the match only to settle our misunderstanding as agreed. Marriage never crossed my mind.

column2: 蘇州の林家が江南の名門であることを知らぬ者はおらん。国に匹敵する富とまでは言わぬが、一方の豪商ではある。娘とて傾国の美女ではないにせよ、花も恥じらう器量の令嬢じゃ。どれほどの名家の若様が望んでも娶れなかったことか。お主に娘を嫌う理由などあるまい！
column3: Who has not heard that the Lins of Suzhou are one of the great families of Jiangnan? We may not be rich enough to rival the state, but we are merchant princes of the region. My daughter may not be a beauty to topple kingdoms, but she is a well-bred young lady as fair as a flower. Countless sons of noble houses have sought her hand in vain. You can have no reason to spurn her!

column2: あの娘のためか？あの娘はお主の何なのじゃ？
column3: Is it because of her? What is she to you?

column2: 彼女は…私と…その…。あまりに突然のことですし、それに家の年長者にも知らせずに、勝手に結婚するわけにはまいりません。
column3: She... and I... well... This has all come so suddenly. Besides, I haven't informed the elders of my family. How could I marry on my own authority?

column2: それももっともじゃ！すぐに人をやってお主の叔母上をお呼びしよう。結納の話はそのときにすればよい。二人ともまずはここに泊まっていきなされ。
column3: A fair point! I shall send someone at once to invite your aunt here, and we can discuss the betrothal gifts then. For now, the two of you shall stay here.

column2: 春蘭！趙のお嬢さんのために西の離れに客間を一つ用意せい。秋菊！婿殿を東の離れへ案内して休んでいただけ。
column3: Chunlan! Prepare a guest room in the west wing for Miss Zhao. Qiuju! Show the young master to the east wing to rest.

column2: はい…旦那様！
column3: Yes... Master!

column2: 若旦那様、ほかにご入り用のものがございましたら、どうぞ遠慮なく私ども使用人にお申しつけください。わたくしはこれで失礼いたします。
column3: Young Master, if there is anything else you need, please don't hesitate to tell us servants. I shall take my leave now.

column2: うわあ…きれいな屋敷だなあ。金持ちの家はやっぱり違うぜ。
column3: Wow... what a beautiful house. Rich families really do live differently.

column2: どうじゃ、わが林家に婿入りする決心がついたかな！？
column3: Well? Have you come around to marrying into our Lin family!?

column2: 霊児、どうしたんだ？顔色があまり良くないみたいだぞ！
column3: Ling'er, what's wrong? You don't look well at all!

column2: わたし…胸が苦しくて、頭が少し痛いんです。でも…大したことはありません。
column3: I... my chest feels tight, and my head aches a little. But... it's nothing serious.

column2: おいおい、病気になったら大変だ。早く寝ろよ…体を冷やすんじゃないぞ。
column3: Oh dear, it won't do to fall ill. Get to bed early... and don't catch a chill.

column2: 逍遥お兄ちゃん、おばあ様が亡くなるときにあなたに言ったこと、覚えていますか……
column3: Brother Xiaoyao, do you still remember what Granny said to you when she died...

column2: 忘れるわけないだろ！安心しろ…お前の母さんが見つかるまで、俺が面倒を見る。約束したことは、絶対に破らないさ。
column3: How could I forget? Don't worry... I'll look after you until we find your mother. I never go back on a promise.

column2: ん？何が言いたいんだ？
column3: Hm? What is it you want to say?

column2: もし…わたしが…その…
column3: If... I... were...

column2: ん？？変なことを考えるなよ。おばかさんだな、何も起きやしないさ…
column3: Hm?? Don't let your imagination run wild, silly girl. Everything will be fine...

column2: 早く寝ろよ。明日の朝になったら、また町へ遊びに連れていってやるから。
column3: Get some sleep. First thing tomorrow I'll take you out to see the town.

column2: 若旦那様、お嬢様をお探しですか？お嬢様はお部屋にはいらっしゃいません。裏の花園で月を眺めておいでです。
column3: Young Master, are you looking for the young mistress? She isn't in her room. She's in the back garden admiring the moon.

column2: 見て！あたしのこの服、似合う？)
column3: Look! Isn't this outfit pretty?)

column2: お、おう…に…似合うよ。
column3: Oh... y-yes, it's pretty.

column2: それだけ…？！せっかく珍しく着てみたっていうのに。
column3: Is that all...?! And here I went to the trouble of dressing up for once.

column2: 林さん、二人だけの話として一つ聞いてもいいか。正直に答えてくれ。
column3: Miss Lin, may I ask you something in private? Please answer me honestly.

column2: 言ってみなさいよ！？
column3: Go on, ask!?

column2: あんた…本気で俺の嫁になるつもりなのか？
column3: Do you... really mean to become my wife?

column2: あたしが嫁に行くんじゃないわ。あんたがうちの林家に婿入りするのよ。
column3: I'm not marrying out to you. You're marrying into our Lin family.

column2: そういうことじゃない。婿選びの試合なんてあまりにいい加減だから、この縁談は無理に成立させなくてもいいって言ってるんだ。
column3: That's not what I mean. I mean a tournament is far too hasty a way to choose a husband. This match doesn't have to stand.

column2: 平気よ、父さんが決めたらそれで決まりなの。
column3: It doesn't matter. What my father says, goes.

column2: その…実は今日擂台に上がってあんたと戦ったのは、ただ誤解を解きたかっただけで、婿選びのことまでは考えてなかったんだ…
column3: Well... the truth is, I only stepped into the ring with you today to clear up our misunderstanding. The marriage part never occurred to me...

column2: ふふ、あたしに勝ったあんたが悪いのよ。今じゃ蘇州中の人が、あんたが林家の新しい婿殿だって知ってるんだから。まさか踏み倒すつもりじゃないでしょうね？
column3: Hee, that's what you get for beating me. Now everyone in Suzhou knows you're the Lin family's new son-in-law. You're not thinking of backing out, are you?

column2: でも、俺たち知り合ってまだ二日だぞ。
column3: But we've only known each other two days.

column2: さんざん言っといて、結局あたしが嫌いなんじゃない！
column3: After all that talk, it turns out you just dislike me!

column2: 違う…そうじゃなくて…。こんなのはあまりに軽はずみな気がするんだ。
column3: No... it's just... I can't help feeling this is all too casual.

column2: あたしは軽はずみな女なんかじゃないわ！自分が何をしてるかくらい、ちゃんと分かってるんだから。
column3: I am not a casual woman! I know perfectly well what I'm doing.

column2: まさか昨日のことをまだ根に持ってて、わざと俺をからかってるんじゃないだろうな？
column3: You're not still holding a grudge over yesterday and toying with me on purpose, are you?

column2: ふふ…どうかしらね？)
column3: Hee... what do you think?)

column2: うちの花園、きれいでしょ？蘇州の町じゃ、うちの庭が一番広いのよ。
column3: Isn't our garden lovely? Ours is the biggest in all Suzhou.

column2: あちこち見て回るといいわ。あんたみたいな田舎者には、きっと目からうろこよ！
column3: Feel free to wander around. A bumpkin like you is sure to have his eyes opened!

column2: 若旦那様ほどの腕前のお方でなければ、うちのお嬢様には釣り合いません。
column3: Only a man of your skill, Young Master, is a worthy match for our young mistress.

column2: 若旦那様、ごきげんよう！
column3: Good day, Young Master!

column2: 若旦那様！旦那様が表の広間までお越しくださいとのことです。
column3: Young Master! The master asks you to come to the front hall.

column2: 旦那様が占い師の先生をお招きになって、若旦那様とお嬢様の八字を合わせていただくそうですよ！
column3: The master has invited a fortune teller to match your birth chart with the young mistress's!

column2: 婿殿、ちょうど良いところへ来た。お主の生まれ年と月日、時刻を教えてくれ。こちらの占い師の先生は、お主と月如の八字を合わせるためにわざわざお招きしたのじゃ。
column3: Son-in-law, you've come at just the right time. Tell me the year, month, day and hour of your birth. I invited this fortune teller specially to match your birth chart with Yueru's.

column2: はあ…私は乙丑の年、臘月十九日の辰の刻の生まれです。
column3: Oh... I was born in the Yichou year, on the nineteenth of the twelfth month, at the hour of the Dragon.

column2: ふむ………どれ、占ってみましょう…
column3: Hmm... let me work it out...

column2: おめでとうございます、旦那様。李の若様とお嬢様は、まさにこの世の一対の璧、天の定めた良縁でございますぞ！
column3: Congratulations, Master. Young Master Li and your daughter are a perfect pair, a match made in heaven!

column2: お二人の八字から見ますに、間違いなく子孫繁栄、富貴栄華でございます。
column3: Judging by their birth charts, they are sure to have a house full of children and grandchildren, and great wealth and honor.

column2: ほっほっほ…それは実にめでたい！
column3: Ho ho ho... that is splendid indeed!

column2: 阿忠、先生を帳場へご案内して謝礼をお渡しせい。
column3: Zhong, take the gentleman to the accounts office for his fee.

column2: はい…旦那様。
column3: Yes... Master.

column2: ほっほっほ、わしは嬉しくてたまらん。これぞまさに林家の果報じゃ！
column3: Ho ho ho, I couldn't be happier. This is truly a blessing for the Lin family!

column2: 婿殿、わが林家は人手が少ない。これからはお主と如児に、林家の男手をたんと増やしてもらわねばのう。はっはっは！
column3: Son-in-law, our Lin family is few in number. From now on we'll be counting on you and Ru'er to give us plenty of strapping sons. Hahaha!

column2: 旦那様、旦那様！誰か早く来てください！
column3: Master! Master! Someone come quickly!

column2: 冬梅、何を騒いでおる！？
column3: Dongmei, what is all this shrieking!?

column2: 妖怪です！西の離れに妖怪がいるんです、ああ恐ろしい！！
column3: A demon! There's a demon in the west wing. It's terrifying!!

column2: 林忠！急いで家の者を集めよ。松明を多めに持ってくるのを忘れるな。
column3: Lin Zhong! Gather the household men at once. And be sure to bring plenty of torches.

column2: はい…旦那様！
column3: Yes... Master!

column2: 妖怪だと？林家堡で暴れるとはいい度胸だ！
column3: A demon? It dares to run amok in the Lin Family Fort!

column2: 妖怪よ！妖怪が出たわ！
column3: A demon! There's a demon!

column2: いったい何が起きたんだ？
column3: What on earth has happened?

column2: 蛇妖よ！半分人間で半分蛇の妖怪が、西の離れの中にいるの！
column3: A snake demon! A demon that's half human and half snake, right there in the west wing!

column2: 霊児！霊児はどこだ？
column3: Ling'er! Where's Ling'er?

column2: 趙さんがいなくなったわ！
column3: Miss Zhao is gone!

column2: 待って！危ないわよ！今は中が真っ暗で何も見えないの。もう人に明かりを取りに行かせたから。
column3: Wait! It's dangerous! It's pitch black in there right now and you can't see a thing. I've already sent someone for lamps.

column2: 霊児はきっとまだ中にいる。俺が助け出してくる！
column3: Ling'er must still be inside. I'm going in to get her out!

column2: あたしも行くわ！
column3: I'm coming with you!

column2: お嬢様！わたくし、あちこち捜しましたが、趙のお嬢様はどこにも見当たりません。
column3: Miss! I've searched everywhere, but there's no sign of Miss Zhao.

column2: 全員に捜させなさい。町の中で見つからなければ町の外まで捜すのよ。蘇州中をひっくり返してでも連れ戻しなさい！
column3: Have everyone go and search. If she's not in the city, look outside it. Bring her back even if you have to turn all Suzhou upside down!

column2: その必要はない！放っておけ！
column3: There is no need! Let her go!

column2: 父さん！どうして！
column3: Father! Why!

column2: お前たち、自分で冬梅に聞いてみるがよい！最初に妖怪を見つけたのはあの娘じゃ。
column3: Ask Dongmei yourselves! She was the first to discover the demon.

column2: 阿梅、妖怪はどこから入ってきたの？趙さんはどこへ行ったの？
column3: Mei, where did the demon get in? And where has Miss Zhao gone?

column2: わたくしがお嬢様のお部屋を掃除しておりましたら、突然、趙のお嬢様の悲鳴が聞こえまして、急いで駆けつけたのです。そうしたら…見てしまったのです…
column3: I was cleaning the young mistress's room when I suddenly heard Miss Zhao scream. I rushed over, and then I saw... I saw...

column2: 李逍遥：\n何を見たんだ！
column3: Li Xiaoyao:\nWhat did you see!

column2: あの蛇妖は…どうやら、趙のお嬢様のようでした。
column3: That snake demon... it seemed to be... Miss Zhao.

column2: 李逍遥：\nお…お前、でたらめを言うな！！
column3: Li Xiaoyao:\nYou... you're lying!!

column2: 阿梅！どうして人にいい加減な濡れ衣を着せるの。趙さんは間違いなく妖怪にさらわれたのよ。
column3: Mei! How can you accuse someone so recklessly? Miss Zhao was obviously carried off by the demon.

column2: わ…わたくし、見たのです…あれの顔を…。あの蛇妖の上半身は人の姿で、その顔立ちは趙のお嬢様にそっくりでした。それから突然、強い風が吹いて……
column3: I... I saw... its face... The upper half of that snake demon was human, and her face looked just like Miss Zhao's. Then all of a sudden a fierce wind blew...

column2: 李逍遥：\n俺は信じないぞ！！
column3: Li Xiaoyao:\nI don't believe it!!

column2: 李逍遥：\nこの件は俺が必ず突き止める。霊児を見つけるまでは、ここへは戻らない！
column3: Li Xiaoyao:\nI'll get to the bottom of this myself. I won't come back until I've found Ling'er!

column2: 阿梅！あんた、怖くて頭がどうかしちゃったんじゃないの？でたらめを言って趙さんに濡れ衣を着せるなんて！？
column3: Mei! Has the fright addled your wits? How can you spout such nonsense and slander Miss Zhao!?

column2: 冬梅にどれほどの度胸がございましても、お嬢様を欺くような真似はとても…
column3: Even if Dongmei had all the nerve in the world, she would never dare deceive you, Miss...

column2: ふん、まったく見損なったわい。あの李逍遥が蛇妖の仲間であったとはのう。こんなことが世間に知れたら、わが林家の面目は丸つぶれじゃ。如児！この縁談はこれで取り消しじゃ。林家は邪魔外道とは付き合わん。
column3: Hmph, how badly I misjudged him. To think that Li Xiaoyao was in league with a snake demon. If word of this gets out, where is the Lin family to hide its face? Ru'er! This marriage is called off here and now. The Lin family does not consort with evil.

column2: いやよ！！！父さんが一度許した結婚なのに、どうして前言を翻せるの？あたし、李兄さん以外の誰にも嫁がないわ！
column3: I won't have it!!! You gave your word on this marriage, Father. How can you go back on it? I'll marry no one but Brother Li!

column2: はあ…娘も大きくなると、引き止めてはおけんのう。
column3: Ahh... once a daughter is grown, there's no holding on to her.

column2: 妖怪よ！本当に妖怪がいるの！趙のお嬢様のお部屋に妖怪が！
column3: A demon! There really is a demon! There's a demon in Miss Zhao's room!

column2: こちらはお嬢様がお住まいの西の離れです。
column3: This is the west wing, where the young mistress lives.

column2: 若旦那様、ごきげんよう！何かご用でしょうか？
column3: Good day, Young Master! Is there something you need?

column2: 若旦那様はやめてくれ！俺と一緒に来た娘の部屋がどこか知らないか？
column3: Don't call me Young Master! Do you know where the room of the girl who came with me is?

column2: あの方は西の離れにお泊まりです。裏の花園の小道をまっすぐ行けば見えてまいります。
column3: She's staying in the west wing. Follow the path through the back garden and you'll see it.

column2: 若旦那様、お嬢様をお探しですか？裏の花園で月を眺めておいでです。
column3: Young Master, are you looking for the young mistress? She's in the back garden admiring the moon.

column2: 若旦那様、ごきげんよう。
column3: Good day, Young Master.

column2: ここが蛇妖の洞窟なのか？
column3: So this is the snake demon's cave?

column2: そうよ、ここよ。
column3: That's right, this is it.

column2: お前はここに残って、俺を待っててくれ。
column3: You stay here and wait for me.

column2: だめよ、あたしも入るわ。
column3: No way. I'm going in too.

column2: お前は女の子なんだ、万一何かあったら…危なすぎるだろ！
column3: You're a girl. If anything were to happen... it's far too dangerous!

column2: あたしに何かあったら…あんたが守ってくれるんでしょ？
column3: If anything happens to me... you'll protect me, won't you?

column2: そりゃ当然だ。
column3: Of course I will.

column2: ふふ、それなら話は決まりじゃない。何をぐずぐずしてるの、行くわよ！
column3: Hee, then that settles it. What are you dawdling for? Let's go!

column2: ねえ、まぬけなコソ泥。こんな真夜中に、どこから捜すつもりなの？
column3: Hey, you thieving blockhead. It's the middle of the night. Where do you plan to start looking?

column2: 林さん！どうしてあんたまで来たんだ？
column3: Miss Lin! What are you doing here too?

column2: 何よ、来ちゃいけないの？何といっても、趙さんはうちでいなくなったんだもの。道義上、あたしにはあんたと一緒に行方を捜す責任があるわ。
column3: What, am I not allowed? After all, Miss Zhao went missing in my home. I'm honor-bound to help you find her.

column2: ありがとう、林さん…。あんたがこんなに情に厚い娘だなんて、知らなかったよ。
column3: Thank you, Miss Lin... I never knew you were such a warm-hearted girl.

column2: なんでまだ林さんなんて呼ぶのよーっ！！
column3: Why are you still calling me Miss Lin!!

column2: じゃあ…どう呼べばいいんだ？
column3: Then... what should I call you?

column2: あたしたちはもう…もう仲間なんだから、これからは兄妹として呼び合うべきよ。あたしが「李兄さん」って呼んだら、あんたは「月如妹」って返すの…
column3: We're already... already companions, so from now on we should address each other as brother and sister. When I call you Brother Li, you should answer with Sister Yueru...

column2: 分かったよ、月如妹…。これでいいんだろ？
column3: All right, Sister Yueru... Will that do?

column2: ふふ…！
column3: Hee...!

column2: そうだ、真面目な話、この辺りはお前の方が詳しい。お前が見たところ、霊児をさらった妖怪はどこへ行ったと思う？
column3: Right, down to business. You know this area well. Where do you think the demon that took Ling'er would have gone?

column2: うーん………
column3: Hmm...

column2: この先そう遠くないところに"隠龍窟"という洞窟があるの。その奥深くに蛇妖の一団が棲みついていて、よくこの辺りに出没するそうよ。若い娘が大勢そいつらに洞窟へさらわれて、行方知れずになってるわ。父さんは何度も志のある人を募って洞窟へ妖怪退治に行かせたけど、一度も成功しなかったうえに、たくさんの死傷者を出したの。だから父さんはあの蛇妖たちを骨の髄まで憎んでいて、趙さんを誤解するようなあんなことを言ってしまったのよ…
column3: Not far ahead is a place called "Hidden Dragon Cave". They say a band of snake demons lives deep inside and often prowls around here. A good many young girls have been carried off into the cave and never seen again. My father has recruited brave men to go in and wipe out the demons many times, but they never succeeded, and many were killed or wounded. That's why he hates those snake demons to the marrow, and why he said those things, misjudging Miss Zhao...

column2: よし、隠龍窟へ案内してくれ。霊児を見つければ、何もかもはっきりするさ。
column3: All right, take me to Hidden Dragon Cave. Once I find Ling'er, everything will be clear.

column2: ひいっ…捕まえんでくれ！このじじいの家にはこんなぼろ薪があるばかりで、お前さんらにやれるような金目の物は何もないんじゃ。
column3: Waah... don't take me! All this old man has is this worthless firewood. I've nothing of value to give you!

column2: じいさん、誤解しないでくれ！俺たちは悪者じゃない。
column3: You've got us wrong, old sir! We're not bad people.

column2: お…お前さんら…妖怪じゃないのかい？
column3: You... you're... not demons?

column2: わしの孫娘が蛇妖にさらわれてのう。いまだに生死も分からん、心配でたまらんのじゃ。
column3: My granddaughter was carried off by the snake demon. To this day I don't know if she's alive or dead. I'm worried sick.

column2: お孫さんの名前は？俺たち、ちょうどその蛇妖を捜しに行くところなんだ。助け出せるかもしれない。
column3: What's your granddaughter's name? We're on our way to find that snake demon right now. We may be able to rescue her.

column2: 本当かい…そりゃありがたい！
column3: Truly... oh, that's wonderful!

column2: 孫娘は暁慧というんじゃ。あの蛇妖のねぐらは西の山のふもとの洞窟の中じゃよ。だが洞窟の中は険しく曲がりくねっておるうえ、毒蛇がうようよ出る。入るのはとても危ないぞ。
column3: My granddaughter's name is Xiaohui. The snake demon's lair is in a cave at the foot of the mountains to the west. But the cave twists and turns over rough ground, and it's crawling with venomous snakes. It's very dangerous to go in.

column2: くれぐれも気をつけるんじゃぞ。これまでにも大勢があの洞窟で命を落としておる。
column3: Do be careful. Many people have already lost their lives in that cave.

column2: きゃあ！？殺さないで！
column3: Aah!? Don't kill me!

column2: あたしはここでお茶をくんだり、物を運んだりしてるだけで、何も知らないんです！
column3: I only pour tea and carry things here. I don't know anything!

column2: あなたは誰？殺さないで！あ…あたし、何も知らないわ。
column3: Who are you? Don't kill me! I... I don't know anything.

column2: 小さな英雄さん、お願いです、あたしたち娘を助けてください！
column3: Young hero, I beg you, please save us girls!

column2: 助けて！こ…殺さないで、お願い。
column3: Help! D-don't... don't kill me, I beg you.

column2: あたしはもともと河東の黒水鎮に住んでいたんです。ぐっすり眠っている間に、気づかないうちにここへ連れてこられました。
column3: I used to live in Blackwater Town, east of the river. I was brought here in my sleep without ever knowing it.

column2: 早くあたしたちを連れ出して！お願いです。
column3: Please get us out of here quickly! I beg you.

column2: お願いです。あたしはこの近くの村から来た者です。どうかあたしたちを助けてください。
column3: Please, I'm from one of the nearby villages. Please save us.

column2: あなたは誰？父さんと母さんに頼まれて、あたしを助けに来てくれたの？
column3: Who are you? Did my father and mother send you to rescue me?

column2: あたしと暁慧は二人とも妖怪にさらわれてきたの。あのとき二人で川辺で水遊びをしていたら、突然妖怪が現れて、あたしたちをこの洞窟へ連れてきたのよ。
column3: Xiaohui and I were both carried off by a demon. We were playing in the water by the river when a demon suddenly appeared and brought the two of us to this cave.

column2: お嬢さん、あんたたちはみんな蛇妖にさらわれてきたのか？
column3: Miss, were all of you carried off by the snake demon?

column2: そうなんです。あのときは本当に怖かったわ！でもここへ来てからは、妖怪はあたしたちに雑用をさせるだけで、ひどいことはしませんでした。
column3: Yes. I was scared out of my wits! Luckily, since we got here the demons have only made us do odd jobs. They haven't hurt us.

column2: 貴様ら、我が洞府に押し入って何をするつもりだ？
column3: What are you doing, barging into my cave dwelling?

column2: お前があの蛇妖か！？霊児を返せ！
column3: So you're the snake demon!? Give Ling'er back!

column2: 霊児とは誰だ？
column3: Who is Ling'er?

column2: 今すぐ引き渡さないなら、俺の剣を食らえ！
column3: Hand her over now, or taste my sword!

column2: 蛇妖は死んだ…
column3: The snake demon is dead...

column2: 妖狐の女：\nあんたたち…何をする気だい？
column3: Fox Demoness:\nYou two... what do you want?

column2: 霊児はどこだ？どこに隠した？
column3: Where's Ling'er? Where have you hidden her?

column2: あたしのところにゃ、外からさらってきた小間使いが大勢いるさ。慧児、珠児、湘児、蘭児とね。けど霊児なんて名の娘は一人もいないよ。
column3: I've got plenty of maids here that were snatched from outside, true enough. There's Hui'er, Zhu'er, Xiang'er, Lan'er... but not one called Ling'er.

column2: 今日の俺は何だってやる覚悟だ。女だからって手を出せないと思うなよ。引き渡さないなら、同じように斬り捨てる！
column3: Today I'm ready to go all the way. Don't think I won't lay a hand on you just because you're a woman. Hand her over, or I'll kill you just the same!

column2: 李兄さん、落ち着いて…。まずはちゃんと聞いてからにしましょう。
column3: Brother Li, calm down... Let's get the facts first.

column2: そんなこと構っていられるか！霊児の髪の毛一本でも欠けていたら、ここの妖怪どもを一匹残らず道連れにしてやる。
column3: I'm past caring about that! If so much as a hair on Ling'er's head has been harmed, every demon here will pay with its life.

column2: 大きな口を叩くじゃないか！
column3: Big words!

column2: お前さん！早く来て、この二人を叩き出すのを手伝っとくれ。
column3: Husband! Come quick and help me throw these two out.

column2: お前さん？
column3: Husband?

column2: 呼んでも無駄だ！入口にいた半人半蛇の妖怪なら、もう俺の剣で死んだ。
column3: Call all you like! That half-human snake demon at the entrance has already died by my sword.

column2: なんだって！？うちの亭主を殺したって？あたしゃ命がけでお前とやり合ってやる！
column3: What!? You killed my husband? I'll fight you to the death!

column2: 石の鍵を手に入れた
column3: Got "Stone Key"

column2: 李兄さん…さっきのあんたの顔つき、すごく怖かったわ。
column3: Brother Li... the look on your face just now was frightening.

column2: もしかしたら…趙さんは本当にここにはいないのかも。
column3: Maybe... Miss Zhao really isn't here.

column2: じゃあ…誰の仕業なんだ？
column3: Then... who did it?

column2: まずはここに妖怪にさらわれてきた女の子たちを助け出しましょう。趙さんの行方は、また一から調べ直すしかないわ…
column3: Let's first rescue the girls the demons brought here. As for Miss Zhao, we'll have to start the search over from the beginning...

column2: あ………ああ、分かった。
column3: A... all right.

column2: 助けて！こ…殺さないで、お願い。
column3: Help! D-don't... don't kill me, I beg you.

column2: 助けて！こっちへ来ないで！
column3: Help! Stay away!

column2: きゃあああ！！！
column3: Aaah!!!

column2: あ…あなたたちは誰！？
column3: Wh... who are you!?

column2: この石の扉には鍵がかかっている…
column3: This stone door is locked...

column2: 阿九：\nお兄ちゃん、いいこと教えてあげる！キョンシーに出くわしたら、命が惜しかったら息を止めるんだよ！
column3: Ajiu:\nHey mister, let me tell you something! If you run into a zombie and want to live, hold your breath!

column2: 子供：\nお母さんが、知らない人と話しちゃだめって。
column3: Child:\nMama says I mustn't talk to strangers.

column2: 漁師：今日は絶好の釣り日和だ。
column3: Fisherman: Fine weather for fishing today.

column2: 村人：\nうむ…今日はいい天気だ。釣りにはもってこいの日だな。
column3: Villager:\nMm... nice weather today. A good day for fishing.

column2: おじさん、俺の友達が病気で、薬引に生きた鯉が要るんだ。釣り道具を貸してもらえないか？
column3: Sir, a friend of mine is ill and needs a live carp as the catalyst for her medicine. Could I borrow your fishing tackle?

column2: おお…いいとも。
column3: Oh... sure.

column2: 使い終わったら忘れずに返しておくれよ。
column3: Remember to give it back when you're done.

column2: 釣り竿をお返しします、ありがとう！
column3: Here's your Fishing Rod back. Thank you!

column2: 釣りは心身を養ってくれる、なかなか良い楽しみだよ。
column3: Fishing cultivates body and mind. It's a fine pastime.

column2: 韓医仙は医術が優れているばかりか、人柄もいい。だからねえ、あの人がこの村の村長になったのは、まさに皆の望みどおりなのさ。
column3: Physician Han is not only a fine healer but a fine man too. So it was just what everyone hoped for when he became our village head.

column2: 韓医仙の娘さんは大した美人でねえ！なお得がたいことに、気立ても父親譲りで優しいんだ。どこの若者が幸運にもあの娘を嫁にもらえるのやら！
column3: Physician Han's daughter is a real beauty! Rarer still, she's as kind-hearted as her father. I wonder which lucky lad will get to marry her!

column2: お母さんが韓医仙のところへ連れてってくれたら、おなかが痛くなくなったよ。
column3: Mama took me to see Physician Han, and my tummy stopped hurting.

column2: この橋の向こうの黒水鎮ではキョンシーが暴れている。絶対に向こうへ行ってはならんぞ。
column3: Blackwater Town beyond this bridge is overrun by zombies. Whatever you do, don't go over there.

column2: これは村長の命令だ。
column3: Those are the village head's orders.

column2: ぼくたち、お馬さんの競走をしてるんだ。誰の木馬が速いか比べっこだよ。
column3: We're playing horse races to see whose wooden horse is faster.

column2: すっごく楽しいよ！
column3: This is so much fun!

column2: 坊や、村長さんの家へはどう行けばいいか知ってるか？
column3: Hey kid, do you know the way to the village head's house?

column2: 知ってるよ！韓おじいちゃんの家はこのすぐ先だよ。
column3: I know! Grandpa Han's house is just up ahead.

column2: あんたたち、ここで何をしてるんだ？
column3: What are you all doing here?

column2: もち米を買うのに並んでるんだよ！もち米がキョンシーに効くって知らないのかい？
column3: We're lining up to buy sticky rice! Don't you know sticky rice wards off zombies?

column2: やれやれ！駱記の米屋の主人が、この非常時につけこんで値をつり上げおって。苦しむのはわしら庶民だよ！
column3: Ugh! The owner of the Luo rice shop is taking advantage of this emergency to jack up his prices. It's we common folk who suffer!

column2: 黒水鎮の屍妖が、うちの白河村まで来て悪さをしやしないだろうか。
column3: I wonder if those corpse demons from Blackwater Town will come and plague our Baihe Village.

column2: 韓村長が情け深く黒水鎮から逃げてきた人たちを受け入れてくれなかったら、あの人たちは今ごろどうなっていたことか。
column3: If Village Head Han hadn't kindly taken in the folk who fled Blackwater Town, who knows what would have become of them.

column2: 押さないでくれ！若いの、買い物は並ぶもんだよ。
column3: Don't push! Young fellow, you have to line up to buy things.

column2: 若いの、あんた、よそから来たんだろ？！知らないかもしれんが、河東の黒水鎮は今キョンシー騒ぎの真っ最中だ。絶対に近づいちゃいかんよ！
column3: Young fellow, you're from out of town, aren't you?! You may not know it, but Blackwater Town east of the river is plagued by zombies right now. Don't go anywhere near it!

column2: 若いの、押すなよ！
column3: Don't push, lad!

column2: もち米がキョンシー相手に本当に効くのかねえ。
column3: I wonder if sticky rice really works against zombies.

column2: 川を鯉が泳ぎ回っている…
column3: Carp are swimming about...

column2: 鯉を一匹釣り上げた
column3: Caught a Carp

column2: 霊児…！！
column3: Ling'er...!!

column2: お二人はこの娘さんをご存じかな？
column3: Do you two know her?

column2: 趙さんはうちに泊まっていたとき、突然いなくなったの。よかった…天は善人を見捨てないのね。
column3: Miss Zhao vanished suddenly while she was a guest at my home. Thank goodness... heaven watches over the good.

column2: 医仙様、ありがとうございます。霊児を助けてくださったのはあなたですね？
column3: Thank you, Physician. It was you who saved Ling'er, wasn't it?

column2: ほっほ、娘が薬草を採りに出かけた折、趙さんが村の外の林で倒れておるのを見つけてのう、それで連れ帰ったのじゃ。
column3: Ho, my daughter was out gathering herbs when she found Miss Zhao lying unconscious in the woods outside the village, and so she brought her back.

column2: 霊児は病気なんですか？ひどいんですか？
column3: Is Ling'er ill? Is it serious?

column2: それは…安心なされ、わしが必ず治してみせよう。
column3: That... rest assured, I will cure her.

column2: 俺に手伝えることはありますか？医仙様のお言いつけなら、たとえ火の中水の中、何でもやります。
column3: Is there anything I can do to help? Whatever you ask of me, Physician, I'll do it though it cost me my life.

column2: ふむ…ではこうしよう。近ごろは病人があまりに多くてのう、薬材の多くを使い切ってしもうた。
column3: Hmm... very well. There have been so many patients lately that I've run out of many medicinal ingredients.

column2: わしのところに、趙さんの体に効くはずの処方が一つあるのじゃが、薬材が足りずに諦めておった。
column3: I have a prescription that should do Miss Zhao's body good, but I had to give it up for lack of ingredients.

column2: お二人にその気があるのなら、ひとつこれらの薬材を手に入れてきてもらえんかな。
column3: Since you two are so willing, may I trouble you to obtain these ingredients for me?

column2: この処方箋を戸口の阿宝に渡して、書いてあるとおりに薬を煎じるよう言いなされ。
column3: Give this prescription to Abao at the door and tell him to brew the medicine as written.

column2: 薬は煎じ上がったかな？
column3: Is the medicine brewed yet?

column2: わしは村長であり、村でただ一人の医者でもある。救える者は一人でも多く救いたいのじゃ。
column3: I am the village head and the only doctor in the village. I will save every life I can.

column2: 母さんはもう妖怪に殺されてしまいました。父さんも大けがをして中で寝ています。もし父さんまで……
column3: My mother has already been killed by the demons, and my father lies inside, gravely wounded. If I lose my father too...

column2: 身寄りもなく一人ぼっちで、どうすればいいんでしょう。
column3: What will I do, all alone with no one to turn to?

column2: 河東の黒水鎮では屍妖が暴れ回っていて、人々はなすすべもなく、この村へ逃げてくるしかなかったのです。けがをした人も多くて、わたしと父だけではとても手が回りません。
column3: Corpse demons are running rampant in Blackwater Town east of the river. The people were helpless and could only flee to our village. Many of them are wounded, and my father and I simply can't keep up.

column2: 隣町の屍妖はますます手がつけられなくなってきた。いつかこの村もやられてしまう。いったいどうすればいいんだ？
column3: The corpse demons in the next town grow more rampant by the day. Sooner or later this village will suffer too. What on earth are we to do?

column2: みんな、どう思う？道士を一人二人呼んで、黒水鎮で法術で妖怪を捕まえてもらうってのは、うまくいくだろうか？
column3: What do you all say? Suppose we hired a Taoist priest or two to perform rites and catch the demons in Blackwater Town. Would that work?

column2: いわゆる「重賞の下には必ず勇夫あり」だ。お触れを貼り出して、わしら白河村のために屍妖を滅ぼした者には、たっぷり褒美を出すとすればいい。
column3: As the saying goes, a rich reward breeds brave men. We could post a notice offering a handsome reward to whoever wipes out the corpse demons for Baihe Village.

column2: 桃木の剣に黒犬の血、それにお札を山ほど用意しないと、キョンシーには立ち向かえないぞ。
column3: We ought to get peachwood swords, black dog blood and a great pile of talismans ready. Only then can we deal with the zombies.

column2: 恐ろしすぎる。屍妖の脅威から逃れるために、この村の者を立ち退かせるべきじゃないかと考えているんだが？
column3: It's too dreadful. I'm wondering if we shouldn't evacuate the villagers to escape the threat of the corpse demons?

column2: 昼間、キョンシーどもが休んでいる隙に、火を放って一匹残らず焼き払ってしまえば、それで片がつくじゃないか？
column3: Why don't we set a fire while the zombies are resting in the daytime and burn the lot of them? Wouldn't that settle it?

column2: 古い書物によれば、なりたてのキョンシーは人が見えないそうだ。このままぐずぐずして、奴らが年を経て人が見えるようになったら、ますます手に負えなくなるぞ。
column3: According to the old books, newly formed zombies can't see people. If we keep dragging our feet until they gain power and can see us, they'll be all the harder to deal with.

column2: 黒水鎮から逃げてきたけが人たちも、キョンシーになってしまうんじゃないか？身を守るためには、いっそ…
column3: Those wounded folk who fled from Blackwater Town... won't they turn into zombies too? To protect ourselves, perhaps we should...

column2: みんなでキョンシー対策を相談しているんだが、まったく頭が痛いよ…。若いの、あんた、何かもっといい手はないかね？
column3: We're all discussing what to do about the zombies, and it's a real headache... Young fellow, do you have any better ideas?

column2: 銀杏果を一つ摘み取った
column3: Picked a Ginkgo Nut

column2: 老農夫：
column3: Old Farmer:

column2: この林には野生の鹿が多いぞ
column3: These woods are full of deer.

column2: 運が良ければ出くわすかもな
column3: With luck, you might meet one.

column2: だがな、鹿は足が速い。
column3: But wild deer are fast. Only

column2: 通り道に罠を仕掛けんと
column3: a trap set on a trail they use

column2: 捕まえられんよ
column3: will catch one.

column2: 薬煎じの童：
column3: Apothecary Boy:

column2: 韓医仙をお探しですか？
column3: Looking for Physician Han?

column2: 家の中にいますよ。
column3: He's inside the house.

column2: 必要な薬材は"人参"、"雪蓮子"、"何首烏"、"銀杏子"、"鹿茸"。それに生きた"鯉"を一匹です。
column3: The ingredients needed are "Ginseng", "Snow Lotus", "Fleeceflower", "Ginkgo Seed" and "Antler Velvet", plus one live "Carp".

column2: 生きた鯉！？
column3: A live carp!?

column2: そうです！この処方は生きた鯉の肝を薬引にしないと効き目が出ないんです。
column3: That's right! This prescription only works with the liver of a live carp as its catalyst.

column2: 手分けして薬材を集めましょう。人参、雪蓮子、何首烏、この三つはあたしが手に入れられるわ。
column3: Let's split up to get the ingredients. Ginseng, Snow Lotus and Fleeceflower: those three I can get.

column2: よし！残りの三つは俺が何とかする。
column3: Good! I'll take care of the other three.

column2: 正午までには戻ってくるわ。
column3: I'll be back before noon.

column2: よく聞いてくださいね："人参"、"雪蓮子"、"何首烏"、"銀杏子"、"鹿茸"、"鯉"です。
column3: Listen carefully: "Ginseng", "Snow Lotus", "Fleeceflower", "Ginkgo Seed", "Antler Velvet", "Carp".

column2: うん…これで薬材は全部そろいましたね。もう少し待っていてください、薬はすぐに煎じ上がりますから。
column3: Mm... now all the ingredients are here. Wait just a little longer. The medicine will be brewed in no time.

column2: この六神丹を病人に飲ませてあげてください。熱いうちに飲むんですよ！
column3: Have the patient take this Six Gods Pill. It should be drunk while it's hot!

column2: 六神丹は我が韓家に代々伝わる秘伝の処方で…薬性は穏やか、滋養強壮に優れ、貧血、風邪、気虚などに著しい効き目があります。ご婦人が服用すれば、血の巡りを整え、安胎の効果もあるんですよ。
column3: The Six Gods Pill is a secret formula handed down in our Han family... It is mild in nature, nourishing and fortifying, and works wonders for anemia, colds, weak qi and the like. Taken by women, it also regulates the blood and protects an unborn child.

column2: ほかの処方もご入り用ですか？この百里四方で、いちばん名が通っているのはうちの韓家薬舗なんですよ。
column3: Do you need any other remedies? For a hundred li around, our Han family pharmacy is the most renowned.

column2: 家の裏の庭に銀杏果の木が一本あります。実を一つ摘めば十分ですよ。
column3: There's a ginkgo tree in the yard behind the house. Picking a single nut will be enough.

column2: 鹿茸と鯉の肝はとても貴重なんです。この二つの薬材も品切れでして。
column3: Antler velvet and carp liver are very precious. We're out of both of those too.

column2: 九陰散を手に入れた
column3: Got Nine-Yin Dust

column2: 九節菖蒲を手に入れた
column3: Got Sweet Flag

column2: 天香続命露を手に入れた
column3: Got Lifesaving Dew

column2: 神仙茶を手に入れた
column3: Got Immortal Tea

column2: 試練の実を手に入れた
column3: Got Trial Fruit

column2: 捕獣罠を回収した
column3: Picked up the Beast Trap

column2: 鹿さんよ、鹿さん！すまないな。俺の友達が病気でさ、あんたの頭の角を薬に借りるぜ。命までは取らないからな。
column3: Brother Deer, oh Brother Deer! I'm sorry. A friend of mine is sick, so I'm borrowing the antlers off your head for medicine. I won't take your life.

column2: 鹿茸を取り、鹿を逃がした
column3: Got Antler Velvet; deer freed.

column2: 趙霊児はまだ意識が戻らない
column3: Zhao Ling'er is still out cold

column2: 趙霊児に薬湯を飲ませた
column3: Gave Zhao Ling'er the medicine

column2: 逍遥お兄ちゃん…お二人とも…
column3: Brother Xiaoyao... both of you...

column2: ああ、まだ起きちゃだめだ。おとなしく横になって休んでろ。
column3: Ah, don't get up yet. Be good and lie there and rest.

column2: ほっほ…構わんよ。趙さんはもう床を離れて歩いても大丈夫じゃ。
column3: Ho... it's all right. Miss Zhao is well enough to get up and walk about now.

column2: わたし、ここに残りたいんです。わたしの法術で、少しは韓先生が村の方々を治療するお手伝いができますから。
column3: I'd like to stay. With my magic, I can help Doctor Han heal at least some of the villagers.

column2: この辺り一帯の村は屍妖にさんざん荒らされ、引っ越せる者はとうに皆出ていった。この村は幸い川に隔てられておるゆえ、今のところ無事でおるにすぎん。お三方は土地の者ではないのじゃから、悪いことは言わん、早く立ち去りなされ。
column3: The villages all around here have been ravaged by the corpse demons, and everyone who could move away left long ago. Our village is only safe for now because the river happens to lie between us. The three of you are not from these parts. My advice is to leave soon.

column2: いいえ…村の方々がこんな苦しみに遭っているのを見ると、わたし…村の方々のために何かしなければと思うんです。医仙様のご恩に報いるためにも。
column3: No... seeing the villagers suffer so, I feel... I ought to do something for them, to repay your kindness, Physician.

column2: 趙さんのその慈悲深いお心、わしはまことにありがたく思う…
column3: Such a compassionate heart, Miss Zhao. I am truly grateful...

column2: 人を治すだけじゃ問題は解決しないだろ！屍妖を退治しない限り、ここの住民にはいつまでも安らぐ日が来ない。みんなで屍妖を退治する方法を考えたらどうなんだ？
column3: Healing people alone won't solve the problem! As long as the corpse demons remain, the folk here will never know a day of peace. Why doesn't everyone think of a way to get rid of them?

column2: はあ…言うは易しじゃ。屍妖はほかの妖怪とは違う。刀も槍も通らず、水にも火にも平気でのう。さらに恐ろしいのは屍毒を放つことじゃ。ひとたび毒気が心臓に回れば、わしにも助けられん。以前は月明かりのない夜にしか現れなんだが、近ごろは真っ昼間でもそこらじゅうをのさばっておる。このままでは、この白河村にも人が住めなくなってしまう。
column3: Ah... easier said than done. Corpse demons are unlike other demons. Blades and spears cannot pierce them, and neither water nor fire harms them. Worse still, they give off corpse poison. Once the poison reaches the heart, even I cannot save the victim. They used to appear only on moonless nights, but lately they roam about everywhere in broad daylight. If this goes on, even Baihe Village will become unlivable.

column2: 村長ともあろう方が、そんな弱気なことを言ってどうするんです。この世のものには必ず天敵がある、妖怪だって例外じゃない。あの屍妖を退治できる者がいないなんて、俺は信じません。
column3: How can you, the village head, talk so despondently? Everything under heaven has something that can overcome it, and demons are no exception. I refuse to believe no one can deal with those corpse demons.

column2: 屍妖に立ち向かえる人を、わたし知っています！
column3: I know of someone who can deal with the corpse demons!

column2: おお！韓さんが知ってるのか？
column3: Oh! You do, Miss Han?

column2: ひと月ほど前、"玉仏寺"の住職の智修大師が屍妖の群れを追い払い、江家の三人の若様の命を救われたのです。その後、三兄弟はそろって出家し、智修大師の門弟になりました。この一件以来、屍妖は二度と玉仏寺に近寄らなくなったそうです。
column3: About a month ago, Master Zhixiu, the abbot of "Jade Buddha Temple", drove off a horde of corpse demons and saved the lives of the three young masters of the Jiang family. Afterward the three brothers all became monks together as Master Zhixiu's disciples. They say that ever since, the corpse demons have not dared go near Jade Buddha Temple.

column2: そりゃいい、今すぐ玉仏寺の和尚に山を下りて妖怪を退治してもらいに行こう！
column3: Excellent! Let's go right now and ask the monks of Jade Buddha Temple to come down the mountain and subdue the demons!

column2: いえ…でも…あなたは…その考えはおやめになった方が。だって…
column3: No... but... you... you'd better give up that idea. Because...

column2: 夢慈、父さんから話そう…
column3: Mengci, let your father explain...

column2: 正直に言うと…わしも人をやって智修大師に山を下りていただくよう頼んだことがある。じゃが…今日まで、住職の方丈に会った者は、誰一人として戻ってこんのじゃ。
column3: To tell the truth... I too have sent people to ask Master Zhixiu to come down the mountain. But... to this day, not one of those who met the abbot has come back.

column2: まさか……その和尚たちが人を食うってのか！？
column3: You can't mean... those monks eat people!?

column2: もちろん違う…皆、坊主になってしもうたのじゃ。
column3: Of course not... rather, they all became monks.

column2: もしかすると…その大師は本当に仏法無辺なのかもな。
column3: Perhaps... that master's Buddhist powers truly are boundless.

column2: いや…少侠、まあ聞いてくだされ。
column3: No... hear me out, young hero.

column2: 娘の夢慈と江家の長男の少雲は、幼いころからの許嫁で、二人はずっと仲睦まじかった。つい先ごろ両家で、夢慈が十六になったら結納を交わそうと話がまとまったばかりじゃ。ひと月前、わしは玉仏寺の智修大師の法力が高いと聞いて、山を下りて妖怪を退治していただこうと考えた。すると少雲と二人の弟が自ら進んで出向いてくれたのじゃが、行ったきり戻らなんだ。わしと娘が何度も訪ねて問いただし、ようやく兄弟三人が出家して坊主になったと知った。この件は今もって、どうにも腑に落ちんのじゃ…
column3: My daughter Mengci and Shaoyun, the eldest son of the Jiang family, have been betrothed since childhood, and the two have always been very close. Only recently our families agreed that the betrothal gifts would be sent once Mengci turned sixteen. A month ago I heard that Master Zhixiu of Jade Buddha Temple had profound powers, and thought to ask him down the mountain to rid us of the demons. Shaoyun and his two younger brothers volunteered to go, and never returned. Only after my daughter and I went many times to inquire did we learn that all three brothers had become monks. To this day, no one can make sense of it...

column2: 聞いてると…この村の災難はほんとに多いんだな…
column3: From the sound of it... this village has more than its share of troubles...

column2: 早く趙さんに薬を飲ませてあげなされ。
column3: Quickly, give Miss Zhao her medicine.

column2: お疲れさまでした…
column3: Thank you for all your trouble...

column2: ほっほ、礼には及ばんよ。これは医者たる者の務めじゃ。
column3: Ho, no need for thanks. It is only a healer's duty.

column2: ほかにも薬材がご入り用でしたら、弟の阿宝にお申しつけください。
column3: If you need any other medicines, you can ask my younger brother Abao.

column2: そこの若いの、この先の林に捕獣罠を仕掛けてあるんだ。この道を行くなら気をつけて、踏まないようにな。
column3: Young fellow, I've set a beast trap in the woods ahead. If you go this way, watch your step and don't tread on it.

column2: 今度こそあの雄鹿を仕留めてやるぞ。
column3: This time I'm going to catch that stag for sure.

column2: 趙さん………余計なことを申すようじゃが、あのお二人はずいぶんあなたを心配しておる。なぜ顔を合わせようとなさらんのかな？
column3: Miss Zhao... forgive an old man for speaking out of turn. Those two care a great deal about you. Why do you avoid seeing them?

column2: わたし…お二人にこのことを知られたくないんです。
column3: I... I don't want them to know about this.

column2: よかろう…安心なされ。わしは引き続き、ほかの者には黙っておこう。
column3: Very well... don't worry. I will go on keeping it from the others for you.

column2: はあ…じゃが…嫁入り前の娘さんが、その…。そのうえ体もひどく弱っておる。世話をする者がおらねば、この先どうやって暮らしていくのじゃ？
column3: Ahh... but... an unmarried girl like you, and... and your body so weak besides. With no one to look after you, how will you get by in the days to come?
Doctor......

column2: まずはわしのところで体を治しなされ。その間によくよく考えてみるのじゃな。
column3: First rest here with me until you are well. Use these days to think it over carefully.

column2: わしの人を見る目に狂いはない。李少侠は、薄情な男ではあるまいよ。
column3: I am never wrong about people. Young Hero Li is not a heartless man.

column2: 若様、お助けいただいたご恩に感謝いたします。どうかわたくしの礼をお受けください…
column3: Thank you for saving me, sir. Please accept my humble bow...

column2: いや、こんなささいなこと、気にしないでくれ。俺たちにとってはお安いご用さ。
column3: No, it's a small thing. Don't give it another thought. It was no trouble at all for us.

column2: わたくしの家はこの先すぐの白河村にございます。お二人さえよろしければ、ぜひお茶を差し上げたく存じます。
column3: My humble home is in Baihe Village, not far ahead. If you two don't mind, you would be most welcome to come for tea.

column2: はあ…狙ってもいないことばかり、うまくいくんだよな…
column3: Sigh... it's always the things you weren't trying for that work out...

column2: がっかりしないで。霊児ちゃんはきっと無事だって、あたし信じてるわ…
column3: Don't lose heart. I'm sure Sister Ling'er will be all right...

column2: どうやら…一から捜し直すしかなさそうだな。
column3: Looks like... we'll just have to start the search over.

column2: 何をじろじろ見てやがる！失せろ！
column3: What are you staring at! Get lost!

column2: 聞こえねえのか？！殴られたいのか？
column3: Didn't you hear me?! Asking for a beating?

column2: 大変じゃ、夢慈がさらわれてしもうた！
column3: Disaster! Mengci has been carried off!

column2: 誰の仕業だ？
column3: Who did it?

column2: 頭目の男は拝月教の長老だと名乗りおった。娘を無事に返してほしければ、趙さんにたった一人で"鬼陰山"まで来させろと言うのじゃ。
column3: Their leader called himself an elder of the Moon-Worship Cult. He said that if I want my daughter back safe, Miss Zhao must come to "Mount Guiyin" all by herself.

column2: ちくしょう…またあのしつこい苗族どもか！
column3: Damn it... those Miao again. They just won't leave us alone!

column2: 韓おじ様、ご安心ください。あの人たちの狙いはわたしです。夢慈お姉さんにひどいことはしないはずです。
column3: Uncle Han, please don't worry. I'm the one they're after. They won't harm Sister Mengci.

column2: 逍遥お兄ちゃん、夢慈お姉さんはわたしの恩人です。わたし、必ず助けに行きます。
column3: Brother Xiaoyao, I owe Sister Mengci a debt of kindness. I must go and save her.

column2: 当たり前だ！今度こそあいつらを一人残らず故郷へ叩き返して、二度とお前につきまとえないようにしてやる！
column3: Of course! This time I'll beat every last one of them all the way back home, so they never dare bother you again!

column2: 頼む、どうか夢慈を助けてくだされ！
column3: I beg you, please save Mengci!

column2: 何者だ？名を名乗れ！
column3: Who goes there? State your name!

column2: わたしが趙霊児です。早く夢慈お姉さんを放してください。
column3: I am Zhao Ling'er. Release Sister Mengci at once.

column2: はっ、趙のお嬢様、どうぞ手前についておいでください。我らが長老は長らくお待ちかねです。ほかの方々は…お引き取り願いましょう。
column3: Yes, Miss Zhao, please follow me. Our elder has been awaiting you for some time. As for the others... kindly go back.

column2: ふざけるな、全員そこをどけ！この俺様が通るんだ、誰にも邪魔はさせないぞ！
column3: Outrageous! Out of my way, all of you! This young master is coming through, and nobody is going to stop me!

column2: ふん、無断で踏み込む者は、殺して容赦せぬ！
column3: Hmph. Trespassers will be killed without mercy!

column2: ほら見なさい！やっぱりあたしの方があんたより早いわ。三つの薬材はもう手に入れたわよ。
column3: See! I'm still quicker than you. I've already got my three ingredients.

column2: どこで手に入れたかって？ふふ…父さんは天下の名高い薬材を集めるのが趣味なの。あたしはこっそり家に戻って、少し持ち出してきただけよ。
column3: Where did I get them, you ask? Hee... my father likes to collect rare medicines from all over the land. I just slipped home and helped myself to a few.

column2: 残りの三つの薬材は全部見つかったの？
column3: Have you found the other three ingredients?

column2: この橋を渡って北西へ行けば"玉仏寺"だ。北東は"黒水鎮"だが、あそこは屍妖がひどく暴れていて、もう誰も住んでいない。
column3: Cross this bridge and head northwest for "Jade Buddha Temple". To the northeast is "Blackwater Town". The corpse demons are so bad there that nobody lives in it anymore.

column2: 南西は"鬼陰山"だ。昔は鬼陰幇と名乗る山賊どもの根城だった。山賊が追い払われた後、近ごろは素性の知れない苗族の一団が現れてな、平気で人を殺す、山賊より恐ろしい連中だ。あんたたちもあの辺りにはむやみに近づかない方がいい。
column3: To the southwest is "Mount Guiyin". It used to be the den of bandits who called themselves the Guiyin Gang. After the bandits were driven off, a band of Miao of unknown origin turned up there recently. They kill without batting an eye and are more fearsome than the bandits ever were. You'd best not go wandering near that area.

column2: 釣り道具一式
column3: A set of fishing tackle

column2: 老人：
column3: Old Man:

column2: 若いの、大恩に感謝するぞ。
column3: Thank you kindly, young man.

column2: 娘もなかなかの器量じゃ。
column3: My girl is fair enough to see.

column2: 恩人殿、娘ではご不満かの？
column3: Would you care to have her?

column2: ええっ！ご老人、そんな冗談はよしてください。俺にはまだ大事な用があるんです。道で不正を見かけて、刀を抜いて助太刀しただけですよ。ほかに用がなければ、これで失礼します。
column3: What! Please don't joke like that, old sir. I still have urgent business to attend to. I only saw a wrong on the road and drew my blade to help. If there's nothing else, I'll take my leave.

column2: あら！恩人様でしたか。まだお名前をうかがっておりませんでした。
column3: Oh! It's you, my benefactor. I haven't yet asked your honored name.

column2: 姓は李、名は逍遥だ。こんなささいなこと、いつまでも気にかけなくていいよ。
column3: My family name is Li, and my given name is Xiaoyao. It was a small thing. There's no need to keep dwelling on it.

column2: ああ…恩人様はわたくしを蛇妖の手から救い出してくださったのに、わたくしはまだ何のお礼もしておりません！
column3: Oh... you rescued me from the clutches of the snake demon, my benefactor, and I haven't yet repaid you!

column2: いいって、いいって！
column3: No need, no need!

column2: お母さんが言ってたよ：夜になるとキョンシーがあちこち走り回るから、外で遊んじゃだめだって。
column3: Mama says zombies run around everywhere at night, so I mustn't go out to play.

column2: はあ…天災も人災も次から次へと起きて、この村にはもう住めなくなりそうだ。
column3: Sigh... with disasters natural and man-made on every side, this village will soon be unfit to live in.

column2: うちの亭主ときたら山へ猟に行って、行ったきり丸一日だよ。昼ご飯に帰ってくることも知らないんだから。
column3: That husband of mine went hunting in the mountains and has been gone the whole day. He doesn't even think to come home for lunch.

column2: ありがとうございました。
column3: Thank you all.

column2: ありがとうございました。
column3: Thank you all.

column2: ありがとうございました。
column3: Thank you all.

column2: ここのもち米はずいぶん高いが、この辺りの村で売っているのはこの店だけなんだ。
column3: The sticky rice here is very expensive, but this is the only shop in the nearby villages that sells it.

column2: 若いの、まだ若いんだから、あちこちうろつかない方がいいぞ。この辺りはキョンシーが出るんだ。
column3: Young fellow, at your tender age you'd better not go wandering about. There are zombies around here.

column2: なんてこった！うちの村には屍妖に立ち向かえる者が一人もいないのか？
column3: Good heavens! Is there no one in our village who can stand up to the corpse demons?

column2: 玉仏寺の和尚たちの助けが得られれば、黒水鎮のキョンシーに立ち向かえるかもしれない。
column3: If we could get the help of the monks of Jade Buddha Temple, we might be able to deal with the zombies of Blackwater Town.

column2: こうと分かっていたら、うちも商売替えしてもち米を作っておくんだった。今ごろは大もうけできたのになあ。
column3: If only I'd known, my family would have switched to growing sticky rice. I could be making a killing right now.

column2: まったく腹が立つ。こんなときにわざともち米をあんなに高く売る商人がいるなんて。
column3: It makes my blood boil. To think there are merchants who'd deliberately sell sticky rice at such a price at a time like this.

column2: あの商人どもは本当に人でなしだ。そのうち子供が生まれても、きっと尻の穴がないぞ。
column3: Those merchants have no conscience at all. Any child they father is sure to be born without a backside.

column2: あんたももち米を買いに来たのかい？うるち米をもち米だと言って売りつけられないよう気をつけなよ！
column3: Are you here to buy sticky rice too? Mind they don't pass off ordinary rice as sticky rice!

column2: おいおいおい！割り込む気か？ぶん殴るぞ！
column3: Hey, hey, hey! Trying to cut in line? Watch it or I'll flatten you!

column2: 兄ちゃんよ、おら、小便を腹いっぱい我慢しとるんだ。ちょっと代わりに並んでてくれんか。おら、用を足してくるから。
column3: Little brother, I'm fit to burst holding my water. Would you keep my place in line for a bit? I need to go relieve myself.

column2: 騒ぐな。
column3: Keep it down.

column2: わしに何の用だ？
column3: What do you want with me?

column2: 今、白河村の人たちはいちばん緊迫した時を迎えている。河東の黒水鎮の屍妖が渡ってくるんじゃないかと、毎日びくびくしてるんだ。
column3: The people of Baihe Village are living through their tensest hour right now. Every day they fear the corpse demons of Blackwater Town east of the river will come across.

column2: キョンシーを防げるのはもち米だけだって、あんたも知ってるだろ。なのにこの機につけこんで米の値をつり上げるなんて、あまりに良心がないんじゃないか？
column3: You know as well as anyone that only sticky rice keeps zombies at bay, yet you seize the chance to drive up the price. Isn't that going a bit too far, even for a man with no conscience?

column2: 乳臭い小僧め！このわしのやることに口を出す気か？お節介が過ぎるわ！
column3: You wet-behind-the-ears brat! You dare meddle in my affairs? You're poking your nose in too far!

column2: これは誰が誰に口を出すとかいう問題じゃない。こんなことが起きれば、誰だって黙って見ちゃいられないさ。
column3: This isn't a question of who's meddling with whom. Nobody could stand by and watch a thing like this.

column2: 恨むなら、商才のない自分たちを恨むんだな。そもそも黒水鎮でキョンシーが出たという噂が流れたとき、連中は人の不幸を面白がるばかりで、まるで本気にしなかった。だがわしはそこに目をつけて、この辺りのもち米をすべて買い占めたのだ。右から左へ流すだけで十倍のもうけよ、はっはっは！
column3: If they want someone to blame, let them blame their own lack of business sense. When word first came that Blackwater Town was plagued by zombies, everyone just gloated over other people's misfortune and paid it no mind. But I saw my chance and bought up every grain of sticky rice in the area. I made ten times my money just by turning it around. Haha!

column2: 商売というのは、このわしのように先を見る目を持ち、好機をつかまねばならん。若いの！よく学んでおけ。
column3: In business you must have foresight like mine and know how to seize the moment. Learn from me, young fellow!

column2: 当店では各種の高級な武器も扱っておる。護身用にいくつか買っていかんかね？さもないと屍妖に出くわしたとき苦労するぞ。
column3: This shop also sells all manner of fine weapons. Won't you buy a few to protect yourself? Otherwise you'll have a hard time of it if you meet a corpse demon.

column2: 若いの、もち米を買うなら、あっちへ行って並びな。
column3: Young fellow, if you want sticky rice, go and line up over there.

column2: 手元が苦しいのかい？物を売りたいのかい？当店は中古品を高値で買い取るよ。
column3: Short of cash? Got something to sell? This shop pays high prices for secondhand goods.

column2: 金がないならどいてくれ。まだ大勢並んでいるんだ！
column3: If you've no money to buy, move along. There are plenty of people still waiting in line!

column2: もち米かい？一袋１００文だよ。
column3: Buying sticky rice? 100 coins a bag.

column2: わたしは河東の黒水鎮から逃げてきた者です。運が強かったおかげで、片足をやられただけで済みました。
column3: I escaped from Blackwater Town east of the river. Luckily fate spared me, and I only hurt one leg.

column2: 腕をキョンシーに咬まれた傷口が、なぜだかたまらなくかゆいんだ。
column3: The wound on my arm where a zombie bit me itches unbearably. I can't think why.

column2: あいたたた…痛いよう！
column3: Owww... it hurts so much!

column2: …ああ、恐ろしい妖怪だった！
column3: ...What a terrifying demon!

column2: 玉児や、玉児、お前はどこにいるんだい？
column3: Yu'er, oh Yu'er, where are you?

column2: …うう！苦しい！
column3: ...Unh! I feel awful!

column2: 若いの、後生だから、その首をちょっと咬ませてくれんか？
column3: Young fellow, have a heart. Would you let me have a little bite of your neck?

column2: こりゃまいった、もち米を買う客がいなくなっちまった。
column3: Now we're in for it. Nobody wants to buy sticky rice anymore.

column2: うわあ…まだ山ほど在庫が売れ残っているのに。
column3: Oh no... and we still have heaps of stock left unsold.

column2: みんなお前たちのせいだ！これでわしは元手まで丸損だ。
column3: This is all your fault! Now I've lost my shirt.

column2: うう………この山のようなもち米は、端午の節句にちまきを作る時期まで買い手がつかんわい。
column3: Boo hoo... nobody will buy this mountain of sticky rice until it's time to wrap rice dumplings for the Dragon Boat Festival.

column2: あんたたち、本当に屍妖を退治したのか？
column3: Did you really wipe out the corpse demons?

column2: ああ。
column3: Yes.

column2: おおっ、すごいな！この吉報を知ったら、みんなきっと大喜びだ。
column3: Wow, amazing! Everyone will be overjoyed to hear the good news.

column2: そろそろ…韓先生にも別れの挨拶をしないとな。
column3: I think... it's time we said our farewells to Doctor Han.

column2: よかった、これでやっと休みが取れる。
column3: Wonderful. I can finally take some time off.

column2: 若いの、その若さでそれほど腕が立つとは見かけによらんな。よくぞ屍妖を倒してくれた。
column3: Young fellow, who'd have guessed that someone so young could be so nimble and strong. You defeated the corpse demons.

column2: 我ら白河村に、ようやく昔の平穏が戻ってきた。
column3: Our Baihe Village has finally regained the peace of former days.

column2: はっ！やっぱり私の目に狂いはなかった。あなたが村に入ってきたときから感じていましたよ。風格は非凡、能ある鷹は爪を隠す、抜群の逸材、その気概は山河を覆うと…
column3: Ha! I knew I hadn't misjudged you. The moment you set foot in the village I could sense it: an uncommon bearing, hidden depths, a cut above the rest, a spirit to cover mountains and rivers...

column2: 実のところ、俺はただ手を出す気がなかっただけさ。そうでなきゃ、お前なんかに出る幕はなかったんだぞ。
column3: The truth is, I simply didn't care to step in. Otherwise you'd never have had your moment.

column2: あなた様の大恩に感謝いたします。我ら白河村の者には、お返しのしようもございません。
column3: We thank you for your great kindness. We folk of Baihe Village have no way to repay you.

column2: 大侠、あなたの像を彫らせてくだされ。そうすれば毎日拝めますからな！
column3: Great hero, let us carve a statue of you, so we can pay our respects to you every day!

column2: あ………施主様…は…その…仏様のお参りに来られたのですか？
column3: Ah... benefactors... are... are you here to pay homage to the Buddha?

column2: 俺たちは、こちらのお寺の智修大師にお目にかかりたいんです。
column3: We'd like an audience with Master Zhixiu of your temple.

column2: ほ…方丈様、人が来ましたーっ！！
column3: A... Abbot, someone's here!!

column2: み…皆様…施主の皆様…どうかここでお待ちを。せ…拙僧が先に中へ知らせてまいります。
column3: Benefactors... good benefactors... please wait here. This... this humble monk will go in and announce you first.

column2: あの和尚、どうしてあたしたちを見たとたんあんなに慌てふためいて、まともに目も合わせられないのかしら？
column3: Why did that monk get so flustered the moment he saw us? He didn't even dare look us in the eye.

column2: はは、出家の身は四大皆空だっていうのに、いきなり美女が二人もお出ましになったんだ。顔色ひとつ変えずにいられるわけないだろ？
column3: Ha! Monks are supposed to be free of all worldly attachments, but when two beauties suddenly turn up, how could he keep a straight face?

column2: ふん、ふざけた顔して！
column3: Hmph, you never take anything seriously!

column2: 霊児…どうしたんだ？
column3: Ling'er... what's wrong?

column2: わたし、このお寺の周りには、どうも…妖気が漂っているような気がするんです。
column3: I can't help feeling there's... a demonic aura around this temple.

column2: 妖気？まさか！ここは仏門の清らかな修行の場だぞ。
column3: A demonic aura? Impossible! This is a pure place of Buddhist cultivation.

column2: わたしにもうまく言えないんですけど…でも…邪悪な妖気ではありません。
column3: I can't quite explain it either... but... it isn't an evil aura.

column2: 施主のお三方、申し訳ありません…。寺の中で少々取り込みがございまして、お客様をお迎えできないのです。
column3: I'm very sorry, benefactors... Something has come up in the temple, and we are unable to receive guests.

column2: おや！智修大師はお寺にいらっしゃらないのか？
column3: Oh! Is Master Zhixiu not in the temple?

column2: い…いいえ、そうではなく。寺の中が少々散らかっておりまして、まだ掃除ができていないのです。施主様、どうかお気を悪くなさらずに…
column3: N-no, it's not that. The temple is in a bit of a mess and hasn't been swept yet. Please don't take offense, benefactors...

column2: ごちゃごちゃうるさいわね！方丈を呼んできなさいよ。それともお寺の中に、人に見せられないことでもあるの？
column3: Stop your blathering! Tell your abbot to come out. Or is there something in the temple you don't want seen?

column2: は…はい！
column3: Y-yes!

column2: 阿弥陀仏…………
column3: Amitabha......

column2: 阿弥陀仏…………
column3: Amitabha......

column2: ここの和尚たちって、どうしてみんな阿弥陀仏しか言えないのかしら。
column3: Why can the monks here say nothing but Amitabha?

column2: うわあーっ！~30
column3: Waaah!~30

column2: おいおい、大師！話せば分かる！
column3: Whoa, whoa, Master! Let's talk this over!

column2: もう我慢ならねえ！このクソガキを叩き斬らせろ！
column3: I can't stand it anymore! Let me hack this little bastard to pieces!

column2: いったいどういうことか、教えてもらえませんか？
column3: Would you mind telling me what this is all about?

column2: このクソガキがおらを騙しやがったんだ！おらはもともと豚殺しでな、毎日少なくとも五斤は肉を食わねえと、体じゅうの調子がおかしくなるんだ。こいつはおらに、ここで坊主になれば毎日食うにも飲むにも困らねえって騙しやがった。ところが来てみたら、まるで話が違うじゃねえか。
column3: This little bastard tricked me! I used to be a pig butcher. I have to eat at least five catties of meat a day or I feel wrong all over. He told me that if I came here and became a monk, I'd have plenty to eat and drink every day. But when I got here, I found it was nothing of the sort.

column2: 食べる物も飲む物も、ちゃんとあるじゃありませんか？
column3: But there is plenty to eat and drink, isn't there?

column2: 米の飯を食って冷めた茶を飲むってことか！？
column3: Eating plain rice and drinking cold tea, you mean!?

column2: あんたの勘違いじゃないかな…出家した者はもともと生臭を食べちゃいけないんだ。
column3: I think you've misunderstood... monks aren't allowed to eat meat in the first place.

column2: 坊主なんかやめてやる、それでいいだろ？
column3: Then I quit being a monk, all right?

column2: さっきおらはやっとの思いで鹿を一頭つかまえて、煮て食って憂さを晴らそうとしたんだ。それなのにこのクソガキめ、鍋ごと肉も汁も全部ひっくり返して捨てやがった。
column3: Just now I finally managed to catch a deer and was about to stew it to satisfy my craving, and what does this little whelp do but tip out the whole pot, meat, broth and all!
A deer...?

column2: そうだ。頭の角が折れて、足にもけがをした雄鹿が寺の中に迷い込んできたんだ。見りゃあ傷口が骨まで腐ってたから、さっさと楽にしてやったのさ！
column3: That's right. A stag with its antlers broken off and a wounded leg wandered into the temple. I saw its wounds had festered to the bone, so I put it out of its misery quick!

column2: 出家を続けたくないなら、還俗して故郷へ帰ればいいじゃない。こんな真似、みっともないにもほどがあるわ。
column3: If you don't want to go on being a monk, why not return to lay life and go home? Carrying on like this is a disgrace.

column2: 帰れるもんなら、とっくに帰ってるさ。
column3: If I could go back, I'd have gone long ago.

column2: どういうこと？
column3: What do you mean?

column2: 方丈様に頭を剃られてからというもの、出家する前のことをおらは何もかも思い出せなくなっちまった。分かってるのは、おらが豚殺しだってことだけだ。おらはただ肉が食いてえんだ！
column3: Ever since the abbot shaved my head, I can't remember a thing from before I became a monk. All I know is that I was a pig butcher. All I want is to eat meat!

column2: おかしいったらないわ、こんな変な人がいるなんて！
column3: How ridiculous. What an oddball!

column2: 施主の皆様、わたくしが方丈様のところへご案内いたしましょう。
column3: Benefactors, allow me to take you to see our abbot.

column2: おら、肉が食いてえ…
column3: I want meat...

column2: こちらが我らの方丈様でございます。
column3: This is our abbot.

column2: 阿弥陀仏………。お三方は何のご用でお越しになったのかな？
column3: Amitabha... What brings you three benefactors here?

column2: 実はこういうことなんです。大師の法力が高いとうかがいまして、山を下りて屍妖を退治し、この地の村人のために害を除いていただきたいのです。
column3: It's like this. We've heard that your powers are great, Master, and we'd like to ask you to come down the mountain, drive off the corpse demons and rid the local villagers of this scourge.

column2: 拙僧は仏門の者、外の俗事には一切関わらぬ。お三方、お引き取りくだされ。
column3: This old monk belongs to the Buddhist order and never concerns himself with the worldly affairs outside. Please go back, all three of you.

column2: 大師、それは違います。出家した者が魔を降し道を守るのは天地の道理、どうして外の俗事などと言えましょうか？
column3: There you are mistaken, Master. For a monk to subdue evil and defend the Way is only right and proper. How can it be a worldly affair?

column2: ふむ………その言葉から察するに、施主にはなかなかの慧根がおありじゃ！
column3: Hmm... judging by those words, you have a real gift for enlightenment, benefactor!

column2: いやいや、とんでもない。
column3: You flatter me, you flatter me.

column2: よかろう。施主が拙僧のために一つ事をなすと約束してくれるなら、拙僧も山を下りて妖怪を退治すると約束しよう。
column3: Very well. If you agree to do one thing for this old monk, I will agree to come down the mountain and subdue the demons.

column2: 天の道にも人の道にも背かないことなら、この李、必ずやり遂げます！
column3: So long as it is nothing that offends heaven or harms the innocent, I, Li, will see it done!

column2: 安心なされ、善いことをするのじゃ。
column3: Rest assured, it is a good deed.

column2: それならお安いご用だ！
column3: Then that's easily done!

column2: ほっほっほ、よし、実によろしい！
column3: Ho ho ho... good, very good!

column2: 智沢、剃刀と袈裟を持ってまいれ。
column3: Zhize, go and fetch the razor and a cassock.

column2: は…はい！
column3: Y-yes...!

column2: 大師、まさか…？
column3: Master, you don't mean to...?

column2: お主を得度させるのじゃ！お主はここで出家して坊主にならねばならん。
column3: Give you the tonsure, of course! You must become a monk here in my temple.

column2: そんな馬鹿な話がある！？絶対にいや！
column3: What kind of deal is that!? No way!

column2: 阿弥陀仏。施主が承知したからには、いやとは言わせぬぞ！
column3: Amitabha. Since you have given your word, benefactor, you have no choice in the matter!

column2: 智杖！こやつらを捕らえよ！
column3: Zhizhang! Seize them!

column2: おや！なぜあがく？坊主になるには髪をきれいに剃り落とすだけでよい。何の苦しみもありはせん。
column3: Oh! Why struggle? To become a monk you need only have your head shaved clean. There is no pain in it at all.

column2: 何だよその条件は？お断りだ。俺はまだ嫁ももらってないんだぞ！
column3: What kind of condition is that? I won't do it. I haven't even got myself a wife yet!

column2: 愚か、愚かじゃ！御仏に帰依した者は死後も地獄に落ちず、西方極楽浄土へ行けるのじゃぞ。何が悪い？
column3: Foolish, foolish! Those who take refuge in the Buddha do not fall into hell after death, and may even go to the Western Paradise. What is wrong with that?

column2: お気持ちだけありがたくいただいておきます。そんなありがたい話は、どうぞご自分のために取っておいてください。この髪型は自分でも気に入ってるんで、お手を煩わせるまでもありません。それじゃ！
column3: I appreciate the thought, truly. Do keep such a blessing for yourself. I'm quite happy with this hairstyle of mine, so there's no need to trouble yourself. Goodbye!

column2: あ………お見送りには及びませんよ。
column3: Ah... no need to see us out.

column2: 入ることはできても、出ることはさせんぞ！
column3: You came in freely, but this old monk will not let you leave!

column2: この妖僧め…蹴り殺してやる！
column3: You fiendish monk... I'll kick you to death!

column2: 逍遥お兄ちゃん、待ってください！
column3: Brother Xiaoyao, wait!

column2: うう………お助けを…もう二度としません…
column3: Boo hoo... spare me... I won't do it again...

column2: どうしてこの小坊主なの！さっきの人たちは、みんなあんたが化けてたの？
column3: It's this little monk!? Were all those people just now you in disguise?

column2: わたくしは達磨大師がお持ちだった数珠が化身したもので、もう九百九十九年修行しております。
column3: I am the transformed spirit of the prayer beads once carried by Bodhidharma. I have been cultivating for nine hundred and ninety-nine years.

column2: 千年もの修行を積んでいるのなら、一心に修練して済度の道を求めるべきです。なぜ自ら堕落して、法力をかさに人を無理やり剃髪出家させ、村の方々を苦しめるのですか！
column3: With a thousand years of cultivation behind you, you should devote yourself to your practice and seek the path of salvation. Why debase yourself, using your powers to force people to shave their heads and become monks, and tormenting the villagers!

column2: わ…わたくしはあの人たちを坊主にしただけで、悪いことをさせたわけじゃありません。お経に曰く、「衆生を普く済度せよ」。また曰く、「人は皆仏性あり」。だから思ったんです。もしわたくしがたくさんたくさんの人を仏門の弟子にできたら、お釈迦様がご覧になってきっと感動なさり、わたくしを天界へ迎えに来て、仏にしてくださると…
column3: I... I only made them monks. I didn't force them to do anything bad. The sutras say: deliver all living beings. They also say: everyone has the Buddha-nature. So I thought, if I could make lots and lots of people disciples of the Buddha, the Buddha would see it and surely be moved, and would come to take me up to the heavens to become a Buddha...

column2: なんてこった…そりゃいったいどこの流儀の修行だよ！小坊主…誰に教わったんだ？
column3: Good grief... what kind of cultivation method is that! Little monk... who taught you this?

column2: わ、わ…わたくしがお経を読んで思いついたんです…
column3: I, I... I thought of it myself from reading the sutras...

column2: 修行の根本は、己を捨てて人を助けることにあります。仏様のおっしゃる無我とは己を捨てること、慈悲とはすなわち人を助けること。それなのにあなたの行いは道に背き、自ら功徳を損なっています。千年の修行も空しく、子供ほどの知恵しかないなんて。このままでは仏になるどころか、先に魔道へ堕ちてしまいますよ。
column3: The root of cultivation lies in giving up oneself to help others. When the Buddha speaks of no-self, it means giving up oneself; when he speaks of compassion, it means helping others. Yet everything you have done runs counter to that and destroys your own merit. A thousand years of cultivation wasted, and you have no more wisdom than a child. At this rate, far from attaining Buddhahood, I fear you will fall into the demonic path first.

column2: え？…菩薩様！あなたは菩薩様だ！
column3: Huh? ...A bodhisattva! You're a bodhisattva!

column2: や、やめてください、わたしは菩薩じゃありません。
column3: P-please don't. I'm no bodhisattva.

column2: うう…感動しました…。こんな道理を教えてくれた人は今まで誰もいませんでした。菩薩様、どうかわたくしを弟子にしてください。
column3: Boo hoo... I'm so moved... No one has ever taught me these truths before. Please, Bodhisattva, take me as your disciple.

column2: これは、わたしのお師匠様が普段から教えてくださったことなんです…
column3: These are things my master used to teach me...

column2: 手柄を立てて罪を償わせてやろう。俺たちはちょうど屍妖を退治しに行くところだ。このちびすけも役に立つかもしれないぞ。
column3: Let him atone for his misdeeds by doing some good. We're just on our way to subdue the corpse demons, and this little squirt may come in handy.

column2: はいはいはい………！お供させてください。屍妖を裏で操っているのが誰か、わたくし知っています。そいつを見つけるお手伝いができます。山のふもとの屍妖のほとんどは、黒水鎮の北にある無縁墓地から来ているんです。そこには隋の時代の将軍塚があって、"赤鬼王"がその地下の血の池に潜んでいます。そいつは邪法で死体を操って人の血を吸わせ、自分の魔功の修練に充てているんです。
column3: Yes, yes, yes...! Let me follow you. I know who is controlling the corpse demons from behind the scenes, and I can help you find him. Most of the corpse demons at the foot of the mountain come from the mass graveyard north of Blackwater Town. There lies a General's Tomb from the Sui dynasty, and the "Red Ghost King" is hiding in the Blood Pool beneath it. He uses dark arts to make the corpses suck human blood, which feeds his demonic cultivation.

column2: おやまあ…なんて邪悪な妖魔なんだ！
column3: My word... what a wicked fiend!
